gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 20?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 20 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent weather models indicate a modest warm spell over southern Germany with daytime highs near 26–28°C, driven by southerly flow ahead of an approaching trough and limited cloud cover initially. Trader consensus clusters tightly on 27–28°C because ensemble guidance shows variability in afternoon convective development and timing of any thundery showers, which can cap or briefly boost surface temperatures by 1–2°C depending on exact onset. Historical August baselines average 23–25°C, but current 500 hPa heights and dewpoint profiles support the upper end of that range; small shifts in boundary-layer mixing or insolation timing differentiate the leading outcomes and sustain near-even implied probabilities. Updated model runs and observational data from the next 12–24 hours will likely refine the distribution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 19 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the LaGuardia Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/ny/new-york-city/KLGA.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

A passing weak frontal system and scattered convective clouds are limiting full radiative heating while light westerly flow prevents strong advection of warmer continental air. Historical August maxima average 23–25 °C, so current conditions represent a modest positive anomaly driven by recent subsidence and drier mid-level air. Traders weigh the latest 12–18 UTC model runs and surface observations against the urban heat-island effect at the official station, where small timing shifts in cloud cover or wind gusts can swing the daily high by 1 °C and decide resolution between the closely matched leaders.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and global models point to a highest temperature in Tokyo on August 21, 2026, most likely in the 30–32°C range, aligning with the market’s leading outcomes of 31°C (41.5%), 30°C (24.0%), and 32°C (23.5%).**

As of August 20, official guidance shows mostly cloudy skies with a 40% chance of showers or thunderstorms, southerly winds around 5–10 km/h, and highs near 30–31°C (86–87°F). These conditions, including increased cloud cover and scattered precipitation, limit solar heating compared with clearer recent days when Tokyo recorded 32.5–32.6°C. Typical August climatology features average highs around 30.9°C, but the current pattern of modest instability and higher humidity supports the market-implied clustering near 31°C. Model consensus remains tight, with limited upside risk above 33°C or downside below 29°C unless unexpected clearing occurs. Traders are weighting the latest JMA and ensemble guidance heavily, as the market will resolve on the official Tokyo station maximum once observations finalize.
